questions.text: What is the shell register map (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: Map as in registers.map (CMD_TYPE 0x00, PARAM1 0x04, PARAM2 0x08, GO 0x0C, RESULT 0x10, RDATA 0x14, TICK 0x18, REFUSED 0x1C, TELEM_ON 0x20, DIRECT_ADDR 0x24, DIRECT_DATA 0x28), 32-bit word accesses.
questions.reason: The request names a test shell and read-back but gives no offsets.
questions.answer:
REFUSED: offset 0x07, WO, reset 0: any write adds one to ERRS
TLM: offset 0x08, RO, reset 0: [0] telemetry on
BANK0..BANK7: offset 0x10, RO, reset 0: the eight registers: ID, SCRATCH0..2, CMDS, ERRS, PERIOD, UPTIME
P1: offset 0x02, RW, reset 0: [31:0] second parameter
TICK: offset 0x06, WO, reset 0: [7:0] added to UPTIME
P0: offset 0x01, RW, reset 0: [15:0] first parameter
CODE: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: [2:0] result of the last command: 0 OK, 1 unknown type, 3 unknown register, 5 write to a read-only register
RDATA: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: value of the last successful read, else 0
TYP: offset 0x00, RW, reset 0: [7:0] command type
GO: offset 0x03, WO, reset 0: any write runs the staged command; reads 0
unmapped: an unused offset reads zero and a write to it, or to a read-only register, has no effect
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
questions.evidence: REFUSED: offset 0x07, WO, reset 0: any write adds one to ERRS

questions.text: Is the refused-command check for write to a read-only register ordered after the register-number range check?
questions.default: Yes, register >= 8 gives result 3 and only 0..7 can give result 5.
questions.reason: The request does not state precedence.
questions.answer: Yes. The spec gives code 3 for any register number above 7 and assigns code 5 only to writes to registers 0 and 4..7, so code 5 can never apply to register 8 or higher. The two checks do not overlap, and the stated order is the range check first, then the read-only check.
questions.evidence: READ/WRITE need register number P0 <= 7 else code 3; WRITE to 0 or 4..7 code 5

questions.text: What happens to a type 1 or 2 command whose param1 has upper bits set (for example 0x0100)?
questions.default: Compare the full 16 bits, so 0x0100 is >= 8 and gives result 3.
questions.reason: Param1 is 16 bits wide but only 0..7 are valid.
questions.answer: Compare the full 16 bits, so 0x0100 is >= 8 and gives result 3.

questions.text: Does telemetry, when on, produce any output?
questions.default: No, only the on flag and PERIOD are kept; no telemetry stream is generated.
questions.reason: The request describes only the flag and period.
questions.answer: No, only the on flag and PERIOD are kept; no telemetry stream is generated.

questions.text: What are the TIMEOUT_CYCLES and BUILD_STAMP values?
questions.default: TIMEOUT_CYCLES = 100000000 and BUILD_STAMP = 0, to be overridden by the shell.
questions.reason: Stated as provided but values are not given.
questions.answer: TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000, not 100000000 as the proposed default states. BUILD_STAMP is not specified, so the proposed default of 0 is not supported and the spec does not settle its value.

questions.text: Is a tick write that coincides with a command finishing handled by applying both?
questions.default: Yes, both updates apply in the same cycle.
questions.reason: The request does not state arbitration.
questions.answer: Yes, both updates apply in the same cycle.
